title: February 1935 photo on Dumaine Street; rehearsals and Ernest Pinn
summary: A February 1935 photo of the band was taken on Dumaine Street near the boxing arena where they rehearsed; Paul praises banjoist Ernest Pinn, who lost his mind and died.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: This is, wait a minute, this is the other, other photograph now. February the 2nd, 1935. 35.
I wonder if they still have negatives up there. Is that Magnolia Studio still here, do you know?
Studio, that's right, I think so. Might be. Now those are bands. You know where this was taken, first of all? Oh, yes, that was taken on Dumaine Street.
This is an ad up here, this Frank's Grocery, Dumaine of Decatur. That's right, that's where I was taken.
Is that where it was? That's where I was taken.
Mm-hmm. It's, that was the arena there where they does boxing. Oh, they had boxing there. Mm-hmm. Yeah. And we'd have rehearsal in that place there. Oh, you rehearsed right there.
Yeah. Is that how you lined up for rehearsal? Or was that for the just the pose?

No, that's just the pose. Oh, okay. But we had a hall there we rehearsed in. Well, they had fellas during the time of this picture there, they had fellas in there couldn't run a C scale. Mm-hmm. But they was musicians. Uh-huh. Now this Professor Carter. Down on the front sitting down in the suit. Yeah, sitting down there. Yeah, sitting down there. This Trapania.
Well, that's Trapania sitting in the, in back of the snare drum, first snare drum on the left. That's right, that's right. Kind of a stout fellow.
Yeah, good picture of him. Mm-hmm. Now you ever heard talk of Oinness Pinn, banjo player? I think so. Well, that's, that, that's what's one fellow. Ernest? Pinn's. Pinn's. Just like Samuel Pinn's.

Pinn's. Yeah, that fella, I'd never seen a man to play with a banjo like he did. He could run all up and down that fingerboard and play anything, any kind of chords, make his own chords. But I'd had to show him the music. Oh, that'd you know. But that fella could execute.
Really could execute. But he lost his mind and he died. It's a tapo, I think. It's there. The second danzo from the left. Mm-hmm. Tapo is there. Anybody else?
